A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AlphaPO research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original alignment experiments on three model families, AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard evaluations, sensitivity analyses, and SPPO continuation results.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds DPO comparisons, a Llama3/ArmoRM configuration, and further training analyses.

M1.justification: The length-normalized alpha reward and margin-based preference loss are unchanged. The reference-policy variant and SPPO continuation procedure were already present in v1, including its appendix.

E1.justification: Both versions use UltraFeedback instruction alignment and evaluate on AlpacaEval 2 and Arena-Hard. Applying ArmoRM additionally to Llama3 changes preference labelling within retained coverage, without adding a task, domain, or evaluation population.

E2.justification: DPO becomes an evaluated comparator across all four model/preference-source configurations in v2 Tables 1 and 4. V1's corresponding benchmark tables compared only AlphaPO and SimPO, so this substantially broadens the comparative evidence.

E3.justification: V2 adds the Llama3/ArmoRM training configuration, explicit DPO configurations, and checkpoint-wise AlpacaEval evaluation alongside KL divergence. Previously reported SimPO/AlphaPO training and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds full alpha-sensitivity curves for Mistral and Llama3, whose optimal alpha values were already stated in v1. Its KL analysis now pairs divergence with checkpoint performance for both models. The existing gamma, reward-distribution, displacement, heatmap, and SPPO analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V1 Table 6 and v2 Table 4 use the same instruction-level standard-deviation reporting and Arena-Hard 95% confidence intervals. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: V2 adds DPO scores and Llama3/ArmoRM results, including AlpacaEval LC values of 47.19, 51.66, and 53.01 for DPO, SimPO, and AlphaPO. Earlier headline AlphaPO/SimPO scores remain unchanged, while sensitivity and checkpoint results expand and KL-curve attribution changes. The new Llama3/ArmoRM DPO Arena-Hard score conflicts: 35.5 in Table 1 versus 33.4 in Table 4.

T1.justification: V2 formalizes existing asymptotic observations in Theorem 3.1, adds the zero-margin case, and introduces the gradient-flow Theorem 3.2 and alpha-threshold Corollary 3.3 with appendix proofs. The original lemma and numerical illustrations are retained. However, Appendix A.4 incorrectly inverts the gradient ratio between Equations 26 and 27.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction newly claim approximately 15%–50% relative improvement over DPO for Llama3 and Mistral. The central reward-shape contribution and claimed improvement over SimPO remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets early preferred-likelihood increases through its new gradient-flow condition. Its KL discussion develops v1's sweet-spot hypothesis into an argument for checkpoint selection and early stopping. The conclusion also identifies reward-shape extensions to DPO and RLHF as future work.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix A.7 adds DPO hyperparameters and their source, plus Llama3/ArmoRM settings. It removes v1's disclosed displacement-analysis test sizes of 1.94k Mistral and 2.99k Gemma2 samples and its SimPO training-log link. Hardware, training-time, and decoding disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Fisch et al. (2024) to connect DPO probability-mass displacement with the new theoretical analysis. It removes the standalone likelihood-displacement related-work paragraph, while retaining the Razin et al. discussion elsewhere. Most research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 substantially condenses and reorganizes the narrative: experimental Sections 4.2–4.7 become one Results section, several explanations and SPPO settings move into appendices, and the conclusion is rewritten. The appendix organization and author list also change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main layout, combines the original benchmark tables into an expanded comparison table, and creates a composite Mistral ablation figure. Numerous plots are relocated or redrawn, and the SPPO result table is replaced by prose retaining its values.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical comparison through DPO, Llama3/ArmoRM, and checkpoint analyses. However, the incorrect ratio in Appendix A.4 undermines the newly claimed alpha threshold, and Tables 1 and 4 disagree on a new DPO result. These reliability problems affect important additions, leaving the net overall quality improvement uncertain.
